questions.question: Which of the following is the universal recipient blood group?
questions.solution:
• **The AB blood group** is the universal recipient blood group.
 
• The blood group of a person is inherited and the blood group depends on the type of antigens on the surface of the red blood cells (RBCs) of the body.
 
• There are two types of antigens, type A and type B which create 4 blood groups, A, B, AB and O.
 
• Since people with blood group AB have both antigens on the surface of the RBCs they can accept any type.
 
• On the other hand blood group O is a universal donor as they have none of the antigens on the surface of the RBCs.

questions.question: Enzymes are _________ that act as catalysts within the living cells.
questions.solution:

• For example, the enzyme protease helps in digestion of protein in the stomach.
 
• The substance which the enzyme works upon is known as the substrate and the converted substance is known as the product of the reaction.

questions.question: The 'Vision 2040' document, released at the Global Aviation Summit 2019, estimates that India will need ______ airports.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The 'Vision 2040' document, released at the Global Aviation Summit 2019, estimates that India will need **200**__ airports.
 
• The document was released by Union Minister of Civil Aviation, Suresh Prabhu at the Global Aviation Summit 2019.
 
• The summit took place on January 15, 2019 in Mumbai.
 
• The document outlined that by 2040 about airways will have 1.1 billion passengers and to cater to them the number of airports in India will have to be doubled to 200 from the current 99.
 
• An investment of $40-50 billion will be required to undertake this huge expansion as the report forecasts that most of the countries airports will be saturated in the next 15 years.

questions.question: ________, a Moroccon traveller who is known for his extensive travels, came to India during the regime of Muhammad bin Tughlag.
questions.solution:
• **Ibn Battuta, **a Moroccan traveller who is known for his extensive travels, came to India during the regime of Muhammad bin Tughlag.
 
• Ibn Battuta was finished with his third pilgrimage to Mecca and then visited Delhi via the Indus River which he reached on 12 September 1333.
 
• He then became acquainted with the Sultan, Muhammad Bin Tughlaq who was the wealthiest Muslim man of that era.
 
• The Sultan appointed Ibn Battuta as a judge, in other words, known as a qadi who enforced Islamic Law on people.
 
• After 6 years he finally left the Sultan's court and travelled to South India and lived under the protection of Jamal-ud-Din who ruled the Nawayath sultanate.

questions.question: 'Red Tape' in an economy refers to _________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• 'Red Tape' in economic terms means **rigid conformity to formal rules.**__
 
• In other words, this means that the market is excessively regulated.
 
• It also means there are too many formal rules that are considered redundant or bureaucratic.
 
• This, in turn, slows down the decision-making process in the market and hurts the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Famous Indian mountaineer **Santosh Yadav** achieved the feat to be the first woman in the world to climb Mount Everest twice and the first woman to successfully climb Mt. Everest from Kangshung Face.
 
• She was born in 1969 and hails from the small village of Adygreg in Haryana.
 
• Her first time to scale Mt Everest was in May 1992 followed by another one in May 1993 she even saved the life of another mountaineer by sharing her oxygen.
 
• In 1999 she led the Indian mountaineering expedition from Kangshung Face and another one East Face of Mt Everest.

questions.question: The Tyndal Effect is due to _____________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Tyndal Effect is caused **by the scattering of light.**__
 
• The light is scattered when it is passed through a colloid which is a term given to a mixture that contains particles (in the range 1-1000 nanometer) of an insoluble substance suspended in a solvent.
 
• The Tyndal Effect makes the beam of light passing through the mixture to be highly visible.
 
• The effect can be easily observed when passing a torchlight through a mixture of milk and water.
